Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- Monitor fever at home with a thermometer. If temperature remains above 37.5–38°C, spikes, or persists with coughing/worsening symptoms, re-contact for re-evaluation.
- Continue supportive, non-antibiotic care for likely viral upper respiratory infection: drink fluids, rest, and use lemon sips (2–3 per day) to soothe throat; avoid combining lemon-sips with other paracetamol-containing products; daytime cough syrup is not recommended; consider a small amount of nighttime cough syrup only if sleep is disrupted.
- Red-flag awareness and plan to re-evaluate: if new/worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, coughing up blood, or inability to maintain hydration or diedal else, seek evaluation promptly.
- Documentation of comorbidity management: maintain regular diabetes and blood pressure checks with the patient’s GP; no changes to chronic meds are documented in this visit unless symptoms persist or worsen.
- If symptoms fail to improve or worsen over 1–2 weeks, a re-assessment is advised; antibiotics may be considered if symptoms persist or bacterial superinfection is suspected on re-evaluation.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 5 days of dry cough and runny nose; nasal discharge described as green; no chest pain or shortness of breath; no coughing up blood.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began ~5 days ago and have been persistent; cough is frequent (approx every 20–30 minutes); no sputum production.
- Associated symptoms: feeling hot to touch with chills; no measured fever; no vomiting; past diarrhoea around onset but currently resolved; good oral intake and hydration; no rashes; muscle aches; occasional wheeze with intense exercise.
- Past medical history: Diabetes mellitus; hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin; lisinopril. Dose reported as “200” for lisinopril; route/frequency not documented; metformin dose not documented.
- Allergies: Hay fever (seasonal allergic rhinitis), no known drug allergies.
- Social history: Lives with partner and a dog; works as an office manager; drinks alcohol occasionally; smoking status not documented.
- Family history: Not discussed.
- Review of systems: Nasal symptoms with green discharge; dry cough; no chest pain; no dyspnea at rest; no hemoptysis; no vomiting; no persistent diarrhea; no headaches or vision changes.

Objective:
- General: Noted by patient to be feeling hot at times; no objective vitals documented in the visit.
- ENT: Nasal symptoms with green discharge; nasal congestion noted.
- Respiratory: Cough described as dry; no productive sputum reported; no shortness of breath at rest; wheeze only with intense exercise; no chest pain.
- Cardiovascular: No chest pain; no edema described; vital signs not recorded.
- GI: Intermittent diarrhea at onset; currently no vomiting or ongoing diarrhea; fluid intake adequate.
- Neurological/Other: No headaches; no rashes; muscle aches present.
- Anthropometrics: Height 5 ft 5 in; weight 65 kg.
- Medications: Metformin; lisinopril (dose documented as 200; route/frequency not documented).

Assessment & Plan:
1. Issue 1: Acute viral upper respiratory infection (possible acute bronchitis)
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute viral upper respiratory infection with possible acute bronchitis. Likelihood: High.
   - Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript/DDx):
     - ACE inhibitor–induced cough. Likelihood: Medium.
     - Acute sinusitis with postnasal drip. Likelihood: Medium.
     - Allergic rhinitis with postnasal drip. Likelihood: Low.
     - Other: Less likely given clinical picture (e.g., lung cancer, GERD-related chronic cough) per DDx, not supported by current history.
   - Investigations planned: None ordered today; home temperature monitoring advised.
   - Treatment planned: Symptomatic management (lemon sips, fluids, rest); avoid daytime cough syrup; limit paracetamol-containing products if using lemon-sips; consider nighttime cough relief only if sleep is disrupted. Re-evaluate if fever persists, cough worsens, or new red flags develop.
   - Referrals: None at this time.

Quality checks (document quality):
- Missing elements: No documented vital signs (temperature, pulse, respirations, blood pressure), no oxygen saturation, no physical examination findings beyond symptom description; no formal meds reconciliation beyond listed chronic meds; smoking status unknown; no immunization history or current vaccination plan documented.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Clear; occasional informal phrasing; essential clinical details captured (onset, nature of cough/nasal symptoms, diabetes/hypertension hx, current meds, red flags discussed).
